title: SLO drift detection and provisioning runbook
author: Marisa Chen
content:
Summary:
This runbook defines detection, validation, and automated/manual provisioning responses for emergent SLO drift across Redwood inference services. It covers drift signal definitions (latency, error-rate, and resource headroom), telemetry queries, triage steps, automated mitigation, and escalation. Use this document as the canonical SRE play for sustained SLO deterioration that appears unrelated to planned deployments or known incidents.

Audience:
- On-call SREs
- Service owners (runtime, routing, model-serving)
- Capacity and infra engineers

Scope and intent:
- Detect SLO drift that is not an isolated spike (10+ minutes sustained or rising trend).
- Prefer automated, reversible mitigations where possible (burst pools, caching, progressive tenant shedding).
- Provide clear gates for provisioning (what metrics to inspect before increasing capacity).
- Ensure actions have owners and post-action validations to avoid overprovisioning.

Key definitions:
- SLO window: 7d rolling with 95th/99th quantiles for latency SLOs and 24h rolling for error-rate SLOs unless otherwise specified per service.
- Drift: a >20% relative increase in error rate or >30% relative increase in 95th latency compared to the 7d baseline, sustained for >= 10 minutes, and not explained by recent deploys.
- Headroom deficit: predicted remaining headroom < 25% under 90th percentile load forecast for the next 60 minutes.

Detection signals (examples):
1) Latency SLO (model-generation route):
- PromQL (95th latency in ms over 5m):
  quantile_over_time(0.95, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service, route)))
- Alert threshold: 95th latency > 1.3x 7d baseline for 10m -> SLO_DRIFT_LATENCY_WARN

2) Error-rate SLO (failed responses / total):
- PromQL:
  sum(rate(http_requests_total{service=\"inference\",status=~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service=\"inference\"}[5m]))
- Alert threshold: error_rate > SLO_target * 1.2 for 10m -> SLO_DRIFT_ERRORS_WARN

3) Capacity headroom (GPU pool utilization + queue length):
- PromQL (simplified):
  (sum(gpu_allocated) / sum(gpu_total)) by (pool) and sum(inference_queue_length) by (pool)
- Alert threshold: predicted_headroom < 25% for next 60m -> CAPACITY_HEADROOM_WARN

Immediate triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Correlate with recent deploys: check CI/CD pipeline events (pipeline id) and model rollouts in the last 30m. If match, follow rollback/canary play instead.
2) Confirm signal fidelity: compare Prometheus, sampling traces (Jaeger), and token-level telemetry from Redwood console.
3) Determine signal type: latency-only, error-only, or mixed. Map to probable root causes: cold KV caches, queueing/backpressure, kernel OOMs, model regression.
4) Identify tenant impact: run the tenant-impact query and list top-5 tenants by request volume and SLO exposure.

Automated mitigations (safe-first, reversible)
- These are triggered automatically when both a SLO_DRIFT_* and CAPACITY_HEADROOM_WARN alert are active and the runbook gate checks pass (no ongoing deployment, infra health OK).
1) Enable short-lived burst pool:
   Command: redwoodctl capacity allocate --pool burst-pool --gpu-type a100-80gb --count 4 --reason \"slo-drift-auto-burst\"
   Validation: within 3 minutes, queue_length drops by >= 40% and 95th latency improves by >= 20%.
2) Activate aggressive prefix/KV caching for eligible tenants:
   Command: redwoodctl cache set --scope tenant:fast-path --policy aggressive --ttl 60s
   Validation: cache_hit_rate increases and effective token-cost drops.
3) Apply temporary per-tenant rate-limits on non-critical tenants:
   CLI example: redwoodctl rate-limit apply --selector \"tier!=enterprise\" --qps 10 --duration 30m --reason \"slo-protect\"
   Validation: system-wide tail latency reduces while enterprise tenants maintain SLO.

Manual provisioning steps (if automated mitigations insufficient):
1) Approve capacity increase (owner: on-call SRE + capacity lead). Use the checklist below before scaling:
   - Confirm no concurrent region-wide cloud incidents (check cloud provider status pages).
   - Confirm autoscaler logs show suppressed scaling or insufficient pre-provisioned capacity.
   - Confirm burst pool exhausted or not configured.
2) Scale GPU pools:
   Command: redwoodctl pool resize --pool inference-default --desired 12 --grace 2m --ticket \"INC-<id>\"
   Notes: prefer incremental increases (20% steps) to avoid scheduling storms.
3) Adjust scheduling affinity to pack latency-critical models onto lower-noise hosts:
   Command: redwoodctl placement set --service inference --policy latency-first
4) Post-scale validation (10 minutes):
   - 95th latency trend should show downward movement within 10 minutes.
   - Queue length and pending requests should drop to < 30% of pre-scale peak.

Escalation and incident creation rules:
- If after 20 minutes from first automated mitigation there is no meaningful improvement, create an incident and notify the following:
  1) On-call SRE (primary) via PagerDuty
  2) Runtime service owner (Slack #runtime)
  3) Capacity lead (email + slack)
- PagerDuty paging policy: severity P1 if error_rate > 2x SLO target for > 15m or 95th latency > 2x baseline for > 15m. Otherwise P2.

Post-action validation and tagging:
- Every provisioning action must include \"slo-drift\" tag on the infra ticket and CLI command. Example: --reason \"slo-drift-auto-burst\"
- Document the action in the incident timeline with metrics before/after and the redwoodctl command executed.

Rollback and cost controls:
- If mitigation degrades correctness (user-visible regressions), immediately roll back:
  - For cache/rate-limit: revert policy changes with redwoodctl cache unset / redwoodctl rate-limit remove --reason \"rollback\"
  - For capacity: redwoodctl pool resize --pool inference-default --desired <previous>
- Automatically set a 6-hour cost guard when burst pools are used: billing-tag \"slo-drift-burst\" with a $ cap. Capacity lead must approve extended costs.

Observability and dashboards referenced:
- SLO overview dashboard: /dashboards/slo/inference-overview (screens to check: latency heatmap, tenant exposure, 5m trend)
- Capacity headroom dashboard: /dashboards/capacity/headroom-pools
- Incident evidence quick-links: distributed trace sample, top-10 token cost by tenant, kernel OOM logs.

Runbook owner and review cadence:
- Owner: SRE Capacity Team (primary: Ibrahim Hassan)
- Secondary owner: Runtime team (Marisa Chen)
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any incident that used this runbook. Add reviewer notes to the runbook page within 7 days after use.

Post-incident analysis guidance (what to include in a short incident review):
1) Timeline of detection -> automation -> manual actions -> resolution (with timestamps).
2) Root cause hypothesis and supporting evidence (traces, heat maps).
3) Cost incurred for burst capacity and justification.
4) Action items: changes to autoscaler, new telemetry, SLO tuning, or capacity reservations. Assign owners and due dates.

Appendix: sample alert rule (Prometheus-style)
- name: slo_drift_latency_warn
  expr: >
    (quantile_over_time(0.95, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{service=\"inference\"}[5m])) by (le, route))[1h:5m])) > (0.95 * (avg_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{service=\"inference\"}[5m])) by (le, route))[7d])))
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    runbook: "/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/slo-drift-detection-and-provisioning-runbook-2026"
